title: Reliability Crew Boarding and Rapid Handoff Guide
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a short, practical playbook for rapidly boarding new reliability crew members and executing time-boxed handoffs for cross-functional SLO ownership. The focus is operational readiness within 30 days and safe, repeatable handoffs for services with latency and availability SLOs.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: new SRE hires, rotational on-call engineers, product owners, and partner platform SMEs.
- Scope: onboarding steps, shift/cadre responsibilities, rapid shadowing plan (30/60/90), a compact handoff checklist for SLO-driven features, communication templates, and acceptance criteria for “ready to own.”
- Not included: full hiring checklist, long-term career development, exhaustive architecture docs (links provided instead).

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
1) New crew member can confidently triage the top 5 production alerts for their service family within 7 days.
2) A reproducible handoff reduces time-to-first-investigation on incidents by 40% (measured over next two months).
3) SLO ownership is transferred with clear rollback and fallback policies documented and tested in a smoke window.
4) Cross-functional partners (product, infra, console) aligned on escalation and runbook ownership.

Roles & responsibilities (compact):
- Incoming crew (new SRE/rotation): complete boarding checklist, shadow 2 oncall shifts, run a mock incident drill by day 14.
- Outgoing owner (service/product SME): deliver handoff briefing, sign off on runbook completeness, run-through of recent incidents and open postmortems.
- Oncall mentor: first point reviewer of runbook updates, gives go/no-go for production access, coordinates first live incident support.
- Product owner/engineer: confirm feature-level SLOs, expected traffic patterns, planned rollouts, and accepted risk thresholds.
- Platform SRE: validate deployment pathways and fallback routes (model variant, region failover, capacity tier).

30/60/90 rapid boarding plan (time-boxed):
- Day 0 (pre-boarding): access requested (internal VPN, KMS test key, read-only billing, pager), invite to team Slack channel and SRE rota.
- Days 1–7: orientation + focused learning
  - Read: concise docs: service README, SLO target doc, recent incident summaries (last 90 days).
  - Do: run the local repro of the service, execute smoke deploy to staging with mentor.
  - Shadow: 1 oncall shift, observe triage flow and post-incident messaging.
- Days 8–21: active pairing and incremental ownership
  - Lead triage for 2 low-severity incidents with mentor present.
  - Implement one enhancement from runbook backlog (e.g., clearer observability query, a new dashboard).
  - Complete SLO verification checklist against production telemetry queries.
- Days 22–30: independent handling + certification
  - Handle at least 1 medium-severity incident solo with mentor escalation available.
  - Run a short tabletop incident with cross-functional stakeholders.
  - Outgoing owner signs off; new owner added to SLO steward list.
- 60/90 day checkpoints: ownership review, quality-of-life changes (automation, alerts tuning), and ramp to proactive experiments (latency budgets, error budget spend tests).

Rapid handoff checklist (must-have items before sign-off):
- Runbook present and up-to-date (link + last-updated timestamp).
- SLO document attached with owner, targets, measurement windows, and alert thresholds.
- Incident postmortem index (last 6) summarized and linked.
- Pager rotation updated and contact escalations verified (phone/pager/SMS test).
- Recovery playbooks for top-3 failure modes (with exact shell commands / runbook buttons).
- Known technical debt and planned mitigations documented.
- Smoke test and rollback steps validated in staging within last 7 days.
- Access matrix confirmed (who has deploy, rollback, DB access).
- Cost and capacity notes for burst scenarios (limits, HV capacity, model variants).

SLO alignment & safety gates for handoff:
- Before ownership transfer, run SLO smoke verification: run a 1-hour synthetic load to validate latency p50/p95 and error rates against production baselines. Capture traces and baseline dashboards.
- If synthetic shows >10% deviation from baseline, postpone handoff and run remediation plan.
- Feature owners must attach rollout policy: canary %, rollback threshold, feature flags, fallback model variant.
- Document fallback routing (region-level or lower-tier model) and automatic fallback triggers.

Communication templates (short):
- Handoff announcement (Slack):
  "TL;DR: @outgoing is handing ownership of service-X -> @incoming on 2026-07-22. Oncall coverage unchanged this week. Key links: runbook, SLO doc, recent incidents. Please ping @oncall-mentor for immediate questions."
- Post-handoff escalation note (email to partners):
  "Ownership change completed. @incoming added as SLO steward. If you notice unexpected regressions in latency or errors, alert the SRE channel and tag @incoming/@oncall-mentor."

Quick incident drill script (15–30m):
1) Trigger synthetic that proxies a failure mode (read-only endpoint latency spike).
2) Engineer-in-training walks through triage: alert -> dashboard -> query -> mitigation (scale, failover, restart).
3) Confirm mitigation and raise postmortem stub with initial notes.
4) Debrief: 10m lessons learned and update runbook if gaps found.

Metrics & acceptance criteria for “ready to own”:
- New owner can: open the correct monitoring query, read the SLO dashboard, and find rollback steps in <5 minutes (measured in drill).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for low/medium alerts during the first 14 days < 15 minutes when the new owner is oncall.
- Runbook completeness score >= 80% against a short checklist (alerts, runbooks, rollback, contacts).

Common risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Knowledge silos (only one person knows critical run commands). Mitigation: require at least two playbook contributors and runbook pair review before sign-off.
- Risk: Premature handoff during active degradation. Mitigation: block transfer if >2 open P1s or active error budget burn > 30% in last 24h.
- Risk: Access gaps (deploy keys missing). Mitigation: pre-boarding access checklist with automated verification step.

Operational artifacts to attach (minimum):
- Links to: runbook, SLO dashboard, incident index, deployment pipeline, access request form.
- Template files: runbook.md template, handoff-slide-template.pptx, postmortem-stub.md.

Next steps and immediate action items (owner in parens):
- Draft runbook refresh for service-X and share with @oncall-mentor (Aisha).
- Schedule two 2-hour shadow shifts across next 10 days (Diego).
- Run SLO synthetic test in staging and capture baseline metrics (Claire).
- Add new owner to the SLO steward group and billing alerts (Omar).

Appendix: Short checklist for outgoing owner to prepare (one-pagers):
- 1-page overview of dependencies and critical circuits.
- Top 5 incident examples with timelines and mitigations.
- Known weakest observability gaps and suggested queries.

Notes to reviewers (why this structure):
This playbook favors short time-boxed confidence activities over long documentation sprints. The goal is measurable readiness rather than perfect documentation. Keep it lightweight and iterate after each handoff with a short retro to capture missing checklist items.

Contact for questions: Aisha Kaur (aisha@redwood-inference.com)
